data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the name Saliim holds a significant meaning. It conveys a sense of protection and security, instilling a sense of comfort and reassurance in those around him. This is emphasized in the historical context of the name's origin, as Saliim is believed to be a descendant of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), who was known for his unwavering devotion to Allah and his belief in Divine Provision. Consequently, the name Saliim has become a symbol of strong faith, protection, and security within the Islamic community.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Saliim is a reminder of the belief in Allah's Protection and security. It is a reminder that the true source of security and comfort lies in the divine, rather than in external or worldly sources. Additionally, it is a call to strive towards a state of safety and security, both spiritually and physically, by following the guidance of Allah and living in accordance with Islamic values.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Saliḥ ibn ʿAli ibn al-Ḥasan, a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the second caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate after Umar ibn al-Khattab. He is also known as Salaam ibn al-Akwa' and Salaam ibn Rabāh. He ruled from 632 CE to 634 CE during which time he continued the consolidation of the Muslim state and the expansion of Muslim territory in the Middle East.
historical_references.context: Rashidun Caliphate, Consolidation of the Muslim state, Expansion of Muslim territory in the Middle East

historical_references.reference: Salaḥ ad-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub, also known as Saladin, was a Kurdish Muslim leader who ruled the Ayyubid Sultanate from Egypt in the late 12th century. He is best known for his role in the Crusades and the reconstruction of Jerusalem. He ruled from 1174 CE to 1193 CE, during the Third Crusade, and was able to successfully repel the Crusaders and reunite the Islamic lands under his rule.
historical_references.context: Kurdish Muslim leader, Ayyubid Sultanate, Reconstruction of Jerusalem, Third Crusade
